text.intro:
Everybody set out the same weekend, each for a different national park, each certain theirs is the better drive.
Four drivers are involved. Determine each driver's distance, ride and snag.
- **Driver**: Gil Ostrander, Hector Salas, Simone and Wendell.
- **Distance** (listed from shorter to longer): 200 miles, 300 miles, 400 miles and 500 miles.
- **Ride**: a hybrid sedan, an old convertible, a rented camper and a minivan with a roof box.
- **Snag**: nothing at all, a thunderstorm, a long line at the gate and a closed pass.
Every driver has a different distance, ride and snag, so within each category every item is used exactly once.
clues: The driver who drives a hybrid sedan covers 400 miles.
The driver who is delayed by a long line at the gate covers 300 miles.
Gil Ostrander and 500 miles are exactly one hundred miles apart in distance order, in one direction or the other.
The driver who is delayed by a thunderstorm falls somewhere between the driver who drives a minivan with a roof box and the driver who drives an old convertible in distance order, matching neither.
Hector Salas does not drive a minivan with a roof box, and is not delayed by nothing at all.
Wendell is not delayed by a closed pass.
Wendell is shorter than the driver who is delayed by nothing at all in distance order.
The driver who drives a rented camper is not delayed by a closed pass.
